newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S GHOSTBUSTERS TARGET PHANTOM STAFF.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S GHOSTBUSTERS TARGET PHANTOM STAFF.

text.p: Government ghostbusters expect to have eliminated most phantom employees from the South African state payroll by the end of the year, a senior Finance Ministry official said on Friday.

The savings from this project will go back to the Treasury. Normally savings from trimmed personnel are used to boost the salaries of remaining Staff, but because these cases involve fraud this would not be the case with the phantom workers.

"I am very confident that by the end of the year we will have a system in place with no spooks or very few spooks still left in it," Director General of State Expenditure Hannes Smit told parliament's finance committee.
He said he believed unofficial estimates of tens of thousands of phantom public servants were exaggerated, adding: "At the end of this time, I don't believe we're going to pick up that many frauds."
But he said anyone collecting salaries of non-existent staff or overpaying themselves would be prosecuted. "It's corruption. It will go to court and we will try to get back what we can," he said.

He said the Department of Finance had entered all 1.3 million public servants on a central database and had started from April 1 to comb through it for anomalies, double entries and phantom employees.
He said the department was looking first at Mpumalanga province where corruption involving housing and drivers' licences has already been uncovered.
Smit said in an interview that provincial departments had already eliminated many phantom posts by the time the central register was implemented on April 1.

"Now we are going through the central register on the basis of identity numbers and authorised staff complements and we are sending payroll details to every supervisor in the field, who must personally check every posts and confirm that these people exist," he said.
